items.title: Its been a while
items.description: I have not posted a video in quite some time. I have been working on a few projects. I just haven't gotten to the end of any of them. I've made a video about what I have been working on. What follows are those projects: Kiln- rolling bed/door I've spent the spring building a solar wood drying kiln. I've gone a little overboard with it. Not so much in size but in functionality. I hope to have a video about this out soon, although I have a lot of footage and it's a long project. My rough edit was almost 2 hours. It's usually about 30 minutes. LOL Star sphere - I was working on a sphere with stars on it for the 4th of July but didn't get it done and then put it aside and I haven't gotten back to it. I would like to finish it. It's a dodecahedron sphere with a star pattern in each pentagon. I ran into trouble with the angle on the pentagons so I need to re-cut the sticks and hopefully make it work. Potter’s head - I know how much everyone loves AI so I want to do a video where I use it as a tool and not a solution. If you're a fan of MASH, the TV show from the '70s and '80s, there's an episode where Margaret and Frank have a bust of Colonel Potter carved and there's a pretty nice image of it in the show. I thought I could use that to create a model and then carve my own version of the Colonel Potter bust. Hey, that's nice! Sword handle A viewer sent me a sword! But it needs a handle so I plan to make a handle for it. I'd like to do a segmented wood turned handle on the CNC. Maybe a handle that has some aspects of a traditional pattern but is made in a different way, made with wood. Fir sphere - I've been gathering firewood all summer. One of the trees I came across had a piece that was a big branch that had been cut years ago and the tree had grown around the cut. I thought this would be interesting to wood turn the chunk itself as had the form of a sphere within it. So I turned two half spheres out of this piece and now it's drying. The plan is to let this dry and reconnect them together and make a sphere. This project probably won't be done until next year sometime as the pieces need to dry. I do have a kiln now to help speed up the drying process Fort Rock - We took a family vacation to Central Oregon early this summer. One of the places we went was Fort Rock, which I have wanted to visit for sometime now. I want to do a topographic map where the more vertical lava sections of Fort Rock are a different colored wood and the whole area is carved and 3D. I think this would make a nice wall hanging Woodtuned bowls - I have some woodturned bowls that I started that I would like to finish. One is a piece of oak that I turned maybe 5 years ago and it has a lot of movement in the wood when it dried. So I'd really like to cut this in half and build a big piece that reforms the bowl into a circle and make a nice finished piece. Another piece that I have is a bowl I made from a large chunk of monkey puzzle tree. It has some really interesting knots in it. It might be fun to do some CNC inlays around or in the knots to make an interesting final project. Deck- Another big project I've worked on and is now finished, or at least the upper part is finished, is a deck on our house. I'm not sure when this video will get done. It is where I got a lot of the wood for the kiln project. I do need to make some furniture for the deck now. Some lounge chairs and a picnic table would be nice. Ornament sphere - I'm not sure what I'm doing for the ornament project at the end of the year. If anyone has any suggestions that could be helpful. My backup plan is to use the leftover pieces from last year's project to make a small sphere that would look like an ornament and be interesting. It just wouldn't be a very long video. items.title: My first hollow form
items.description: I have been wanting to play around with woodturning hollow forms. This is a form that is similar to woodturning a bowl except that the opening at the top is very small so it makes a form that is more hollow than it is open. I received a delivery of fir and maple wood a couple of years ago and I have been slowly turning that wood. I started with a piece of fir and an old hollowing tool that I had bought years and years ago that had just been sitting on the shelf waiting for me to pick it up. This attempt was successful but not as hollow as I would have liked. The opening was somewhere between what would be considered a hollow form and a bowl. I then received the new hollowing tool from Carter and Son Toolworks woodturning tools and this was a much better tool than what I had. I worked on some of the maple from the same delivery of wood and made a handful of hollow forms. After doing this, I realized that when you turn a bowl, you turn off the material with the screw holes from where the faceplate attaches when you initially wood turn the form. But when you do a hollow form, those screw holes are still there. So I was trying to think up a way to solve the problem of the screw holes that I had in my woodturning. I thought about cutting them out with the CNC machine. Then I came up with the idea of making a ring of segmented pieces and cutting that ring into the top of the hollow forms with the CNC. This would make a new smaller opening for the hollow form and cover up the holes left by the screws from the faceplate. This worked really nicely and it makes a beautiful collar for the hole for the hollow form. I really like this technique. I now have two maple hollow forms with walnut collars or frames around the opening of the form. items.title: Upgrades to the CNC
items.description: I've made some upgrades to the CNC machine. Avid CNC sent me some new parts to install. The biggest change is upgrading the control box and the control software. I'm going from Mach 4 to CNC 12. This new control software should be more stable than Mach 4 was, and I'm finding this to be true. I also changed the computer that runs the software. Because this computer is much smaller, I cut down my computer cabinet to a lower height. Now really only the screen sits above the work surface. I like this better as it doesn't block the view of the CNC machine from where I'm sitting at the computer. Some small additions that I made were a new tool height setter and a new dust shoe that work a lot better than the old system. I also installed a new crosshair laser which allows me to set the 0,0 point very easily on the machine. I also got a ring light to go around the spindle. This will illuminate the work as I set up jobs. Overall, the updates have been working well. I have made a first project using the new updates. This project is a bread slicing board. items.title: Most Complicated Ornament Yet
items.description: For this year's Christmas ornament I thought I would make a wreath, and in making this form, I thought I would make a wood turned torus. I decided I would add stripes to make it appear like a candy cane design. I use the sticks from the PDX airport flooring project to make a wood turned segmented torus. I made 73 12 segmented rings that I cut a 5° angle in and stacked these rings together to make the torus. I then cut it into six pieces and added a striped ring in the space between the cut pieces of the torus. I glued everything back together again and that gave me a stripe candy cane pattern within the donut shape. I wood turned this glue up on the lathe. I glued the torus to a circle that I had cut out on the CNC machine and then attached this circle to the chuck on the lathe. I turned as much as I could with that setup. Then I glued a second circle to the other side of the torus with hot glue and I turned the torus around and held it from the other side. This allowed me to turn the other parts of the torus that I couldn't reach on the first pass. After I sanded it to 600 grit and added walnut finish, it came out really nice. items.title: Wood Flooring Turned Mallets
items.description: I have made more mallets. I have found a new source for wood to make the mallets. This wood was destined for the Portland airport renovation. A good friend of mine owns The Zena Forest Products that also makes the wood flooring tiles for the new airport renovation. I was able to scavenge a dumpster full of the rejected pieces for this flooring. I have glued these pieces together to make the heads for a series of Carver's mallets. The mallets also use the radial finger joint I've been using in the past to connect the head of the mallet with the handle of the mallet. Once the blank for the mallet is all glued up, I wood turned it into a mallet shape. items.title: What is the Point of this Bowl?
items.description: I had a maple bowl blank that I made in 2012. This bowl blank had a lot of material on the bottom part of the bowl and I thought it would be good to try something I've been thinking about for a while. I wanted to add legs to the bottom of a bowl. I used a radial box joint that I cut on the CNC machine to add three walnut legs. I then carved the excess material away forming three pointy legs. It looks a little spooky but I like it. items.title: How I Fixed My Kitchen Mixer
items.description: I fixed my KitchenAid mixer. Last spring, my mixer stopped being able to mix any thick dough. It would “chatter” as it tried to mix. I watched a few videos on how to fix a KitchenAid mixer and felt I could do it. I also found the parts I would probably need. I pulled the top off of the mixer and got to the gears and the motor. I found a gear that was definitely stripped. Five or six teeth were missing on the gear. I was able to order this exact gear and replace it with new grease. I also found a pin that goes through the shaft that holds the main gears in the mixer. This pin was broken so I made a new one on my metal lathe. I put everything back together and it has been working nicely now for almost a year. Other mixer fixing videos https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lQoC6UvQTPI&t=555s https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bxj1mflNH3Y Tools used in this project can be found at http://www.frankmakes.com/ To see upcoming projects follow me on social media Patreon https://patreon.com/user?u=16151185&utm_medium=clipboard_copy&utm_source=copyLink&utm_campaign=creatorshare_creator&utm_content=join_link Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/frankmakes.bsky.social Instagram https://www.instagram.com/frank.howarth/ Facebook https://www.facebook.com/FrankMakes 0:00 (introduction) 0:29 (disassembly) 3:11 (pin) 4:20 (assembly) 7:17 (conclusion)

items.title: Making A Garden Storage Cabinet
items.description: I've made an outdoor garden storage cabinet in our carport. We had an area in our carport that was just filling up with garden tools and garden paraphernalia. I wanted to tidy this area up. I had some pieces of poplar and some free plywood I had obtained that I used to make the cabinet. I made the sides and top out of rail and style frames. The back is a sheet of 1/2-in plywood. I made a base out of a frame of poplar that the whole cabinet sits on. I attached adjustable feet to the base so I could keep everything level as the floor of the carport slopes away from the house for drainage. I also made a top out of the scrap pieces of poplar. items.title: Making An Ornament (2024)
items.description: This year's Christmas ornament is a sphere with a top and bottom finial. The sphere has 24 segments running from top to bottom, making a striped pattern. In the sphere, I have three accent pieces which are circles each made from a 12 segmented piece. Two of them are a star pattern and the third is a little bit of an experiment with a more random pattern. The main body of the sphere is made from maple and walnut stripes. The accent pieces are made with plum and holly wood. The top and bottom finials are made from walnut. I like this ornament because it is playful and also looks familiar. items.title: Making Jar storage
items.description: I have been canning a lot of tomatoes over the past few years. I now have a lot of jars both empty and filled with tomatoes and other things. I need a place to store all of these jars. I found a wall in the back of our basement that seemed like a good place to make a thin but very dense wall of shelves for my jars. Last winter, we cut down a pine tree just outside the house. I cut the trunk of that tree into slabs and feel that the wood is now dry enough for this project. I made five bays of shells. Each bay is two vertical pieces with dados that receive the shelves that hold the jars. Each shelf is the width of a jar plus a little bit for space. And each shelf is six jars wide plus a little bit for space. I made a system on the outer face of the shelves that consists of a clip and a bar. The clip holds the bar against the shelf at about the center of the height of the jars. This bar will keep the jars in place in case we have a little earthquake or the cats get a little too crazy around the jars. items.title: wood tuning a fir bowl
items.description: I acquired a free load of fir from a tree not too far away from us. I got a couple of nice logs that I slabbed from this lot. I also got several shorter pieces of fir. I cut them in half to make bowl blanks. I have woodturned two of them into nice sized bowls. In this video, I go through the process without very many edits. You see most of what I do to go from a short log to a finished bowl. The one difficulty I had was getting a good surface on the green fir. I ended up just woodturning with a very sharp 40/40 bowl gouge and not trying to sand the surface. I finished the piece with walnut oil and hope it dries to a nice usable bowl. items.title: Fast cherry bowl
items.description: I have made a small cherry bowl with a racing stripe. I rough turned this bowl years ago and it has dried into an oval shape with a tiny bit of bark intrusion in one spot. To finish this bowl, I cut it in half along that bark intrusion and added two strips of maple and one strip of walnut wood between the two halves. I then glued the strips and the two halves of the bowl back together again. Then I wood turned the piece into a final bowl with a racing stripe. items.title: Spike the Bowl
items.description: I've made a bowl with spikes on the outside. I used the detail that I use on my carvers mallets to attach the spikes to the bowl. This entails carving a radial joint on the CNC machine. Half the joint is on the end of a piece of walnut and the other half on the cherry bowl. The two pieces are glued together. This bowl has 15 spikes. Once the two parts are glued together, I then have to carve the walnut and the cherry to reveal the pattern in the joint between the two pieces. I really like how it turned out. It's a simple round bowl on the inside and a very spiky, pointy surface on the outside. items.title: Coffee Table Makeover
items.description: We decided the coffee table I made a little over a year ago wasn't quite big enough. My idea to enlarge the coffee table was to cut the coffee table in half lengthwise and add another piece to the width. Luckily, I had another piece of wood from the same tree, so the piece that I added matched very well. I also reshaped this new piece to match the curvy shape of the underside of the table. The other thing we wanted to do was make a more interesting top for the table. I thought about a couple of different designs. One being two pieces of wood with a curved seam between the two. Another being a zipper pattern made with segmented pieces of wood. But what I ended up doing was an M.C. Escher inspired piece that transforms between fish and birds. It makes a very beautiful coffee table top. The top just sits on top of the table in a giant mortise which is a cutout on the underside of the new top. The top is made with maple and walnut to give a strong contrast between the light and dark wood. items.title: Making Mars out of Cherry
items.description: I have made the planet Mars from a dodecahedron made out of cherry wood. The dodecahedron is made out of pentagons that have the terrain of Mars carved into them. I put the pentagons together to make the sphere of the planet. I did a similar project about the moon a few months ago and in that project I had trouble keeping the seams between the pentagons small. In this Mars project, I was able to hold the pentagons with a mortise and tenon on my table saw jig. This allowed me to cut the angle between the different pentagons along the sides of each pentagon by holding them from the center instead of from the edge. This minimized the seam between each of the pentagons creating the final form of Mars.
